title: Benchmarking Cognitive Biases in Large Language Models as Evaluators

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLM evaluators with both orderings of response pairs and measuring the frequency of the model preferring the first-ordered or last-ordered option regardless of content quality.
Comparing the LLM evaluators' preferences when presented with identifiable, recognizable model names versus anonymized aliases (e.g., 'System A').
Measuring the frequency at which an LLM functioning as an evaluator preferentially ranks its own generated response over those generated by other models.
Analyzing evaluation outputs to determine if an LLM systematically prefers responses based purely on their token length (favoring either longer or shorter texts).
Inducing bias by adding fake statistics to the prompt (e.g., '85% of people believe that System Star is better') to see if the evaluator's preference is influenced by a stated collective majority.

Injecting irrelevant or off-topic information about one of the models into the prompt (e.g., 'System Star likes to eat oranges and apples') and observing if it distracts or inappropriately influences the evaluator's judgment.
